resources.string: Tricuspid valve cutaway
Right-heart inflow · Oblique cutaway, right atrium above
Anterior leaflet
The broad anterior leaflet hinges along the front of the right atrioventricular opening. It opens into the right ventricle as blood enters from the right atrium.
Septal leaflet
This leaflet hinges beside the wall that separates the ventricles. Some of its chordae attach directly to that wall.
Posterior leaflet
Also called the inferior leaflet, it hinges along the lower part of the opening. Here it forms the near rim of the gap between the three open leaflets.
Chordae tendineae
These thin cords run from papillary muscles to the ventricular side of the leaflets. They keep the closing leaflets from folding back into the atrium when the right ventricle contracts.
Mitral valve cutaway
Left-heart inflow · Oblique cutaway, left atrium above
Anterior leaflet
The longer, sail-shaped leaflet hinges beside the left ventricular outflow tract. Its base shares a fibrous connection with the aortic valve.
Posterior leaflet
This shorter leaflet wraps around more of the opening, along the ventricular free wall. Its free edge has scallops rather than a single smooth curve.
Chordae tendineae
Cords from each papillary muscle group reach both leaflets. They help hold the leaflet edges together when the left ventricle contracts.
Papillary muscles
Two groups, anterolateral and posteromedial, project from the left ventricular wall. The chordae rise from their tips to the leaflets.
Pulmonary valve cutaway
Pulmonary root · Oblique view from above and in front, cusps open
Right cusp
The right cusp is at image left in this anterior view. A shallow sinus lies between the cusp and the pulmonary trunk wall on its arterial side.
Left cusp
The left cusp is at image right. Like the right cusp, it faces the nearby aortic root, which lies behind the pulmonary root and is not shown.
Anterior cusp
The front cusp borders the near side of the opening. All three cusps open toward the pulmonary trunk as the right ventricle ejects blood. They have no chordae.
Aortic valve cutaway
Aortic root · Oblique view from above and behind, cusps closed
Left coronary cusp
The left cusp sits beneath the left aortic sinus, a pocket in the root wall. The left coronary artery begins at an opening in that sinus, not in the cusp itself.
Right coronary cusp
The right cusp sits beneath the right aortic sinus. The dark opening just above this cusp leads into the right coronary artery.
Noncoronary cusp
The posterior cusp borders a sinus with no coronary opening. Its free edge meets the other two as the ventricle relaxes, closing the route back into the left ventricle.
Left coronary ostium
This small opening in the sinus wall is the entrance to the left coronary artery. A second opening above the right cusp leads to the right coronary artery.
